kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Sales and other operating revenue of $80.0B, down from $81.1B a year ago; total revenue including other income was $82.3B

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Down from $1.72 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $1.71, excluding identified items

kpis.label: Energy Products earnings
kpis.note: Refining and fuels earnings (GAAP), up from $0.4B a year ago as refining margins surged; $2.9B on an adjusted basis

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: Cash flow from operations was $12.7B; $9.5B was returned to shareholders in dividends and buybacks

oneTimers: Impairments of $1,700M — including a $640M charge to optimize materials and supply inventory — cut GAAP earnings, partly offset by a $720M gain on the sale of assets in non-U.S. Energy Products.
Tax-related items added $288M and restructuring charges cost $64M. Total identified items were a net $755M drag; excluding them, earnings were $7,256M, or $1.71 a share.
otherDetail: Income from equity affiliates of $966M plus other income of $1,303M, less the $108M of net income attributable to noncontrolling interests — outside partners' shares of joint ventures — leaving $2,161M.

segments.name: Upstream
segments.note: Oil and gas production — crude and gas sold to outside buyers. Most output goes to ExxonMobil's own refineries, so earnings are the better gauge: $3.5B, down from $6.5B a year ago on lower crude prices, even as production hit a record 4,988 thousand barrels a day.

segments.name: Energy Products
segments.note: Refining and fuels — gasoline, diesel and jet fuel sold worldwide, by far the largest sales line. Earnings jumped to $3.4B from $0.4B a year ago as refining margins surged.

segments.name: Chemical Products
segments.note: Basic chemicals and plastics that go into packaging, cars and everyday goods. The segment swung to a $281M loss from $120M of earnings a year ago on weak chemical margins.

segments.name: Specialty Products
segments.note: Higher-value products — lubricants, basestocks and specialty fluids. Earnings were $682M, down from $746M a year ago.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Sales and other operating revenue in Corporate and Financing that is not part of a reportable segment — the small remainder so the segments add up to the company total.

takeaways.text: Energy Products earnings jumped to $3.4B from $0.4B a year ago as refining margins surged — without it, the quarter would have looked much worse, since Upstream earnings nearly halved on lower crude prices.
takeaways.title: Refining rescued the quarter

takeaways.text: Upstream earned $3.5B, down from $6.5B a year ago on lower crude prices, even as production hit a quarterly record of nearly 5.0 million barrels a day, with Guyana passing 700,000 gross barrels a day and advantaged assets now 59% of production.
takeaways.title: Upstream earnings nearly halved

takeaways.text: ExxonMobil declared a first-quarter dividend of $1.03 a share, payable March 10, 2026 — its 43rd straight year of raising the annual dividend. It returned $9.5B to shareholders in the quarter ($4.4B of dividends and $5.1B of buybacks).
takeaways.title: Dividend up for a 43rd year

verdict: ExxonMobil's profit fell 15% to $6.5 billion as lower oil prices cut Upstream earnings nearly in half, but surging refining margins lifted Energy Products earnings to $3.4 billion and the company still returned $9.5 billion to shareholders.
